nodes.label: SimulatorManager: macOS MenuBarExtra App
nodes.rationale: A macOS SwiftUI MenuBarExtra app for inspecting and managing apps installed in local Apple simulators. Explicitly not an iOS app; visionOS simulators appear in the UI but app discovery differs by platform, so platform-specific discovery branches are intentional.

nodes.label: macOS 15.0+ Deployment Target
nodes.rationale: The app target and LSMinimumSystemVersion are both 15.0. The project-level MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET of 14.0 is only an inherited default the targets override, so it must not be quoted as the requirement.

nodes.label: xcodebuild Build and Test Commands
nodes.rationale: Build and test go through the SimulatorManager scheme in SimulatorManager.xcodeproj; single tests are selected with -only-testing since the suite uses Swift Testing.

nodes.label: SwiftFormat and SwiftLint Build Phases
nodes.rationale: Formatting and linting run automatically as Xcode build phases (SwiftFormat then SwiftLint) so style is enforced on every build rather than relying on contributors remembering to run them; manual invocation stays available.

nodes.label: Signed and Notarized Release Build
nodes.rationale: build.sh wraps `bundle exec fastlane release`; a .env with signing/notarization secrets is required. `bundle exec fastlane build` produces an unsigned debug build only.

nodes.label: Lightweight MVVM with Service-Based Filesystem Logic
nodes.rationale: Views stay thin and presentation-only; discovery, monitoring, reset, and filesystem logic live in services and managers so bugs are fixed at the service/manager layer instead of being patched in views.

nodes.label: App Entry Dependency Wiring
nodes.rationale: SimulatorManagerApp is the single composition root wiring shared state and dependencies (DeviceManager, SimulatorResetService, Settings) so injection points stay in one place.

nodes.label: DeviceManager as Central Coordinator
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for simulator devices, device types, and recent installed apps, so views and view models never derive device state independently.

nodes.label: AppDiscoveryService Plist Scanning
nodes.rationale: Scans simulator folders, reads plist metadata via CustomPropertyListDecoder, and constructs app and app-group models — keeping raw filesystem/plist parsing out of view models.

nodes.label: Debounced Device App Monitoring
nodes.rationale: A main-actor service manages per-device AppFolderMonitor instances built on FolderMonitor (FSEvents). Updates are debounced 3s because FSEvents fires in bursts during installs, and an app only counts as updated when its contentModifiedAt moved forward, avoiding spurious 'recent app' churn.

nodes.label: Device as a Reference Type
nodes.rationale: Device is deliberately a reference type with mutable @Published state for apps and app groups so monitoring updates propagate in place; converting it to a value type requires a clear architectural reason.

nodes.label: Centralized CoreSimulator Path Derivation
nodes.rationale: SimulatorPaths centralizes CoreSimulator directory path derivation so paths are reused rather than re-hardcoded at each call site.

nodes.label: Centralized Settings via UserDefaults Suite
nodes.rationale: Settings centralizes user preferences in one UserDefaults suite; new preferences are added there rather than scattering UserDefaults access across the codebase.

nodes.label: Intentionally Disabled App Sandbox
nodes.rationale: com.apple.security.app-sandbox = false in SimulatorManager.entitlements is required for direct filesystem access to CoreSimulator directories under ~/Library. Re-enabling sandboxing would break app discovery, so it must not be turned back on.

nodes.label: Dual Observation Pattern Split by Layer
nodes.rationale: Two observation systems coexist on purpose: view models are @MainActor @Observable classes held with @State (injected dependencies and non-UI state marked @ObservationIgnored), while the model/service layer stays ObservableObject with @Published and Combine consumed via @StateObject/@ObservedObject. The split is preserved deliberately — neither side should be converted to the other without a clear architectural reason.

nodes.label: Combine Subscription and Main-Queue Delivery
nodes.rationale: Subscriptions are stored in Set<AnyCancellable> (marked @ObservationIgnored inside an @Observable view model) and always .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main) before assigning observed state, so UI updates happen on the main queue.

nodes.label: Thin, Presentation-Only Views
nodes.rationale: Discovery, monitoring, reset, and filesystem logic belongs in services/managers, not views, so behavior stays testable without a UI host.

nodes.label: Protocol Seams with Constructor Injection
nodes.rationale: New services used by view models are defined behind a protocol (DeviceManaging, DeviceAppMonitoring) with constructor injection so tests can substitute mocks. These seams must not be removed.

nodes.label: Defensive Filesystem and Decode Handling
nodes.rationale: Missing files/folders and decode failures are handled defensively and logged with os_log rather than crashing, because simulator directories change underneath the app while it runs; .DS_Store and similar noise is filtered out.

nodes.label: Recent Apps Dedupe, Sort and Cap
nodes.rationale: Recent-apps behavior in DeviceManager must stay: dedupe by bundle identifier plus device UDID, sort by most recent timestamp, cap list size. App changes are diffed by bundle identifier and an app counts as updated only when contentModifiedAt moved forward.

nodes.label: Issue-Named Branch and Worktree Convention
nodes.rationale: Every feature branch and worktree is named <issue-number>-<slugified-issue-title>, matching what GitHub generates from 'Create a branch for this issue'. Feature work is never committed directly to develop; if no issue exists one is created first, since the issue is the spec carrying context, required behaviour, knock-on effects, a verification checklist, and explicit out-of-scope. dependabot/* and release/* keep their tool-generated names.

nodes.label: Pull Request Workflow Against develop
nodes.rationale: PRs open against develop, never main, with 'Closes #<number>' so issue and project board item close on merge. A PR's head branch cannot be changed after opening, so a wrongly named branch means closing and reopening the PR — the branch name must be right before the first push.

nodes.label: GitHub Project Board Item Tracking
nodes.rationale: Maintainers add each issue to project board 1 under owner Heckscheibe and set its Status; outside contributors skip this because the board is not writable by them.

nodes.label: Swift Testing Conventions
nodes.rationale: Swift Testing (@Suite, @Test, #expect) is used instead of XCTest. Mocks live in SimulatorManagerTests/Mocks and factories in Helpers/TestDataHelpers; Combine-driven tests must await async propagation before asserting on @Published state, and DeviceManager or view model changes must cover sorting, deduplication, and edge cases.

nodes.label: Minimal, Architecture-Preserving Changes
nodes.rationale: Favor minimal, localized changes that preserve the current architecture; fix at the service/manager layer, keep protocol seams used for tests, and do not replace Combine-based model/service flows with another state management approach unless explicitly requested.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions go through `graphify query`, `graphify path`, and `graphify explain` first because they return a scoped subgraph far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output. GRAPH_REPORT.md is reserved for broad architecture review, and `graphify update .` keeps the graph current at no API cost.
